The [official redb design](https://github.com/cberner/redb/blob/master/docs/design.md) describes coherent MVCC reads and delayed page reuse. The exact pin's db.rs::ReadableDatabase::begin_read captures a committed version; transactions.rs::ReadTransaction::open_table clones the transaction guard into each table. Consequently dropping the top-level read transaction does not release a capture pin while tables/iterators still own it. A paused serialized capture is a concrete first profile; concurrent capture would require explicit pin lifetime, retained-page/disk-growth and apply-latency evidence. A raw live-file copy does not follow from the coherent logical-read guarantee.

The [current redb4.4 WriteTransaction contract](https://docs.rs/redb/latest/redb/struct.WriteTransaction.html) documents savepoint retention and transaction durability. The pin confirms persistent savepoints keep old pages alive and restore_savepoint rejects a different Database tracker. A savepoint is not a portable complete snapshot artifact. One Immediate transaction can publish a replacement authority cohort and its current-artifact descriptor together, but neither this API nor first-party W bounds engine page/transaction residency or disk headroom. Do not hold one writer and call the existing recovery::validate, which begins another writer; shared validation must use the same proposed tables or an isolated staging store before the active transaction.

[Rust io::copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/fn.copy.html) streams until EOF and may use Linux-specific descriptor copying. That supplies no application byte cap, framing check, checksum or portable no-copy performance guarantee. Explicit row/chunk/total limits, checked counts and complete EOF remain necessary. Hash the exact canonical stream incrementally; do not allocate a full-image Vec or use an uncapped read_to_end. A stream limit ending exactly at its allowance is not itself proof of genuine EOF; the selected grammar must distinguish complete framing from trailing input without overflowing a limit+1 calculation.

[BufReader](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/struct.BufReader.html) may retain unread bytes; replacing/unwrapping readers mid-stream can lose them. Use one counted stream context across framing and account for any read-ahead. [BufWriter](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/struct.BufWriter.html) has a buffer whose requested capacity is not an exact-allocation promise; drop suppresses flush errors. Use an explicitly paid buffer, inspect flush/into_inner errors, and separately establish durable file custody if files are chosen. [File](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/struct.File.html) sync calls expose errors ignored by close, and try_clone shares the seek position. Cloning a descriptor does not create independent snapshot-reader cursors. External file publication additionally needs an explicit directory/cleanup protocol, beyond buffered flush.

The freshly fetched [OpenRaft0.9.25 state-machine contract](https://docs.rs/openraft/latest/openraft/storage/trait.RaftStateMachine.html), also checked in cached v2.rs, distinguishes durable-state-machine and durable-snapshot profiles: the former need not persist snapshot artifacts across restart. Installation must expose the installed snapshot before return. Durable immutable custody is therefore the proposed product recovery choice, not a universal upstream requirement. While a snapshot remains current, later applies cannot silently regenerate different bytes under its old metadata; explicit new capture may replace both. Metadata-only markers and the old scalar/opaque-membership experiment do not demonstrate complete product retrieval/restore.

A concrete direction worth selecting is isolated unserved input staging plus bounded atomic import into the existing active database, retaining immutable canonical chunks for caller-stream export. This works with the consumed-Database/fault-backend seam without inventing a filesystem directory hidden inside an opaque Database or an escaping redb reader. A future OpenRaft bridge can export the artifact into its owned SnapshotData. Artifact tables/descriptor must be versioned, whitelisted and excluded from captured authority to prevent recursive snapshots; original FWSS/FWMV/FWSC and all ROWS0..7 stay exact. Previous artifact retirement/read lifetimes and legacy-layout disposition need explicit decisions. No such inventory is selected here.

The staging owner should retain exclusive immutable custody after receiving input; do not validate a mutable external stream and then reread it as proof. Malformed received bytes must leave healthy active authority usable. Reusing active checked() would incorrectly turn incoming semantic defects into a fatal active-store Corrupt. Isolated source validation preserves this distinction; real active engine corruption/I/O/uncertain commit still follows fencing and reopen. Target admission/membership/schema limits must also apply to imported content; a stage admitted under a larger profile cannot bypass the active captured profile.

Logical resource units must distinguish input/capture rows, full key/value/frame bytes, chunks and actual buffer capacities from semantic visits, cross-probes and decoded owners. Existing recovery redirects owned reads into cumulative C: decoded physical key, scope/record/outcome/history/policy and neighboring owners all count, as do repeated policy/schema visits. One-row streaming is not a reason to reset that account. Price active+stage namespace owners, retained metadata or typed membership U, chunk/read/write buffers and any copied key/value simultaneously. A sequential maximum is sound only after the earlier buffers/typed owners actually drop. Direct borrowed stage-row insertion may avoid a first-party copy, but engine copying and residency remain separate. Stage point/range indexes should support semantic cross-checks; repeatedly scanning the whole artifact/chunk stream per record would add hidden quadratic work. Include staging validation, active import, artifact copy and cleanup visits in the whole operation's named work units.

Purge stays a required ordered successor. Current log metadata has no purged boundary and current recovery audits0..A. Snapshot-aware startup needs a verified complete base S, its full control/M/time/digest/lineage, then retained audit(S,A] and committed replay. Snapshot-local A alone is not evidence of durable commitment; capture/install coordination must establish actual provenance. Publish a recoverable artifact/state anchor before destructive log purge, with exact full-ID boundaries and a two-database crash protocol. None of this is supplied merely by a checksum or successful stream copy.

Prospective correctness criteria: independently packed complete cohorts; capture S, apply later entries, retrieve unchanged S; binary identities, full membership/learners/addresses, leases/fences, original outcome versions/status/expiry, history, due/FIFO and foreign placements; valid1MiB inline fields and full262,162-byte policy; row/chunk/EOF/reordering/duplicate/namespace and bidirectional-index corruption; one-short healthy limits; source-read/sink-write errors preserving active state; actual engine failure after the intended publication phase; and real kills around durable activation, followed by strict reopen proving complete old or complete new authority. Do not confuse completed-call kills with power-loss. The exact pin's tests/crash_consistency.rs reconstructs durable versus volatile bytes at a sync boundary and checks retained baseline state; it was read locally, not fetched or executed. Cached OpenRaft Suite::transfer_snapshot exercises metadata/state transfer, and is not a substitute for these product fault/resource tests.

Prospective measurement criteria, not results: record capture/receive/semantic-validation/import/durable-publication durations separately; bytes read/written, reached rows/chunks and repeated probes; first-party retained capacity alongside process RSS, active/stage engine-cache configuration and disk growth; paused apply duration and post-restart validation cost. Use identical validated datasets spanning many small rows, large rows/policies, repeated same-lane records and multiple explicit stream-buffer sizes, with warm/cold states reported separately. Check complete digest/cohort equality on every measurement run. Report distributions and failures on Linux and macOS independently, with exact pin/build/durability/profile recorded. Compare alternative buffering/copy choices only after a correct baseline exists; no throughput, zero-copy, RSS ceiling or cross-platform gain has been measured here.

Purge uses one existing count/full-wire census for every affected prefix row PLUS the first reached retained neighbor, before shared decode/checksum. The count and full70+body bytes are charged without copying either keys or RaftLogEntry owners; a missing next row has no row/wire fee. It neither invokes complete reopen validation nor scans the unrelated suffix. The validation function returns, dropping all iterators/value guards, before inclusive-upper retain_in and the atomic anchor/state update in the SAME Immediate writer. Logical workspace includes bounded metadata, not redb's internal freed-page vectors, COW/rebalance/cache or I/O. The native engine deletion is a second walk; no timing or constant-native-memory result is inferred.

FWLS state output is at most160B, covered by the existing fixed2048 operation allowance. The source/target account handoff is coherent. New transactions start scalar counters at0; source.carry_from(target) precedes source work, target.carry_from(source) precedes target work, and each resumes from the other's latest scalar frontier. copy() does this before each table open/iteration/row-copy phase and carries the last EOF step back. compatible() carries before each source/target read phase. Max therefore preserves sequential cumulative work here; it is not used to merge independently advanced disjoint accounts after the fact. One PolicySchemaCharge spans target validation, incoming revalidation, compatibility and final publication within each method. D must prospectively include their descriptors, owned component leaves, workflow type/worker, scope/header/isolation and other actual decoder owners; wire length alone is not a truthful slot allowance. Reserve configured R/S/C before decoder ownership, then admit the real D and any additional held reply/plan/context under W. A checked count before a loop is a work bound only if the selected immutable profile is checked before that loop; the entry's own scan/head hints are not that profile. Schema, Claim-work, steps and cumulative R/S/C continue across one driver invocation, including repeated reads whose earlier donors have died. Dropping a donor reduces a native live peak, not an already spent logical counter.

The current pure claim/selection.rs reads every provided logical head before selection, merges due candidates in domain order, distinguishes exhaustion from scan/claim limits and has a borrowed SameSnapshot continuation only for zero-write use. claim/apply/admission/{consumed,selected}.rs and decision.rs verify canonical/index/placement/mode/encoding authority and charge nested output owners before command/token construction. The proposed observed reducer must factor those duties onto real reached records, actual membership facts and true heads; neither bypass them nor manufacture unobserved complete maps. Gather stable admitted record owners first, then construct maps borrowing those owners. Do not keep a borrowed row from an engine cursor while growing its backing Vec or publish a borrowed resume after consuming the writer. The lease response must be independently bounded and owned through the actual commit, then moved to the reply. Point-gate NonFresh paths must remain before Fresh policy/time/query/head reads and preserve the originally retained body, time, log and expiry.

P2 resolves a necessary distinction. Semantic merged-scan/head counters belong to the requested query scope and the due<=effective-now frontier, with the exact state/priority resolution still to be frozen. Unrelated workflows and future rows do not consume those semantic units. Actual storage work is broader: every reached unrelated key, bound/reseek, end/empty probe, lookahead, decode, canonical read and performed head probe pays the immutable operational accounts. The physical due ordering puts type/partition after priority/time, so a narrow requested scope can traverse a large unrelated prefix. Any-lane discovery must establish all relevant real nonempty heads; it cannot substitute a speculative all-placement-by-configured-state empty Cartesian product. Explicit finite logical-lane None probes count when actually performed. Running or unscheduled true FIFO heads remain blockers even if they have no eligible due row. An incomplete discovery/frontier at BudgetEnd proves neither emptiness nor RangeEnd. A paid upper-bound jump using the existing lane-key grammar may skip followers; an implementation that physically visits80 followers must charge those80 visits even if it counts only one semantic head.

I reread the entire current state/redb/cursor.rs: candidate() reconstructs scope/prefix/lower bounds, opens ROWS and reseeks per row; matches() owns a canonical record and, for FIFO, owns its real head, validates them, then drops both before returning only DueOrder borrowed from the cursor position. A subsequent tx.record call owns/charges another result. The returned-row maximum hides internally filtered visits and cannot become the source merged-scan count. Changing that public cursor's contract is not implied by a new Claim observation API. Preserve its existing continuation, fence and BudgetEnd behavior.

Full policy ownership remains material. read/point.rs admits the installed-policy logical R tariff2048+216*actual encoded bytes before materialization. transaction/load.rs already deduplicates types, carries one schema account through full policy reads and projections, and retains both complete policy owners and owned retry/mode projections; projection descriptors/copies debit S separately. Reusing that pattern in Claim is appropriate, not a newly measured optimization. The projection is not full governance. If a typed donor and its independently bound encoded bytes arrive from outside this verified read path, the existing no-allocation complete_policy_value_owned_bytes helper measures U=2048+512*typed occurrences+typed variable bytes+independent encoded length. It grants no content correspondence. Keep the same schema account through verification and do not substitute P(tiny encoded bytes) for a large unverified typed owner. No cross-transaction policy cache or omitted full governance fields are justified by a same-guard reuse argument.

P1 is necessary for policy edits: canonical record keys lack workflow type, and an unscheduled parallel record can have neither due nor FIFO membership. Current recovery resolves index mode from the installed policy. Therefore a mode edit needs bounded canonical-record discovery, with all reached unrelated records and performed probes/decodes charged, followed by atomic complete reindex/activation or an explicitly selected authoritative migration protocol. Secondary due/FIFO indexes alone cannot prove every newly FIFO member. A new type index would require its own writes, bidirectional recovery, snapshot/layout and work contract; none is silently introduced here. Small affected-result count is not a bound on discovery. Refusal must leave the previous policy, records, indexes, history, outcome and control coherent together.

For startup/replay, keep the actual existing one-point/body pool and Q=512+t+g+r. The adopted Normal outer overlap B+max(actualJ+Q,512+Q+driver.W) remains the reference, with actual Claim decoder/reply lifetimes demonstrated rather than assumed equivalent to record batches. Full frame/body/scope/stamp validation and the actual log-point pre-copy bound remain distinct from a cheap header. A Claim driver cannot gain a second body owner, retain policy/record windows across unrelated phases or reset work merely by moving between audit and replay helpers.

Primary sources and concrete unselected optimization candidates

I checked current primary Rust std and redb documentation online, and the adopted engine source locally. Successful std pages reported1.99.1; the repository toolchain is1.99.0, so current documentation is research rather than a fabricated exact-toolchain run. Successful docs.rs latest redb pages reported4.4.0. Exact version/raw GitHub fetches in this consultation were unavailable with fetch/cache errors; I do not describe them as successful reads. Adopted facts were independently checked in local redb4.4.0 commit7061f7e60d4573311c0636e161d417b93e9fd2b1 from Cargo.lock, in table.rs, btree_iters.rs and btree_cursor_range.rs/btree_cursor.rs. Registry docs alone do not prove equality to that git revision.

1. Compare a function-local admitted raw observation loop against the current cursor's per-row reseek. In the adopted engine, range construction copies encoded bounds to owned Vecs, creates cursor state and can retain read pages. A new local loop can hold one Table/range, use shared borrowed-table canonical/index probes, collect only admitted stable owners and explicitly drop every row guard/range/table before publication. No self-referential cursor, nested same-table open, cloned range or full-cohort map is needed. This may reduce opens, bound copies and repeated seeks; measure it. Longer-lived guards/page pins, writer residence, COW/page traffic and error/overread precedence are costs to compare. Cloning Range is not a free cursor operation: the pinned implementation owns bound/path state and page references. An upper-bound lane seek must use the shared codec and pay its own bound/seek/end work. The official [ReadableTable range contract](https://docs.rs/redb/latest/redb/trait.ReadableTable.html#tymethod.range) is consistent with treating iterator/guard lifetime as part of the design, not a promise of constant-cost seeks or physical memory usage.

2. Preserve same-writer deduplicated full-policy capture and borrowed query keys, and investigate repeated decode/projection only where a measured profile identifies it. The existing load.rs already deduplicates actual types; do not claim that saving again as a new gain. A future Claim reader can reuse an admitted capture/projection for the same actual type/revision/generation instead of reloading it per selected record, while still paying the actual owners and every required semantic validation. If consumed-record publication changes a relevant view, reuse needs a proof for that change. The [BTreeMap borrowed-key API](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/collections/struct.BTreeMap.html#method.get) supports avoiding an independently owned query key only when borrowed ordering agrees with stored ordering. It does not make map nodes or result projections free. Full policy versus retry/mode/governance semantics must remain explicit; no retry-only shadow store is proposed.

3. Compare direct exact-sized record/history encoding into a transaction reservation with the existing publication.rs encode-owned-Vec-then-insert path, only as a later selected experiment. The pinned Table::insert_reserve validates individual key/value and combined geometry and exposes an exact requested mutable region; insert replaces the supplied value through the engine. Before reserving, compute checked exact wire length, preserve the actual3GiB individual/3.75GiB pair ceiling, pay key/output C, and prove byte-for-byte fields/checksum equivalence and safe transaction abort on an encoding failure. All mutable guards must die before later operations. A reservation removes neither engine page/transaction allocations nor durability work; conservative logical C need not change merely because a first-party intermediate Vec disappears. The [official reserve API](https://docs.rs/redb/latest/redb/struct.Table.html#method.insert_reserve) is an applicable mechanism, not a throughput or allocation measurement. No current value encoder/API or fee changes here.

The [Vec allocation guarantees](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/vec/struct.Vec.html) support exact known-count prospective reservations and reuse of already paid capacity, while allowing allocator excess. try_reserve_exact does not promise exact physical capacity. Vec-to-Box slice conversion avoids movement/reallocation under its documented len==capacity condition; a general conversion may discard excess capacity and reallocate. Growing observation/command/filter buffers and existing pointer/capacity-preserving owners therefore get no blanket Box recommendation. Any immutable-final-spine experiment needs its own lifetime/growth/measurement case; logical tariffs are not std ABI sizes or allocator predictions.

Proposed correctness and portable measurement controls

These are future test/benchmark criteria, not executed probes or a new dependency/instrumentation selection. First compare the observed path with the existing complete reference for the EXACT same query universe, effective time, original versions/fences and full policy. Cover priority2/1/0, binary/tied due order, explicit/Any scopes, real empty lanes, running/expired/unscheduled blockers,80/deeper followers, narrow queries behind large unrelated prefixes, true exhaustion versus exact scan/head/work stops, lease token/expiry bytes and zero-write continuation restrictions. Use full raw cohorts/reopen and independent response expectations around each optimization. Include reached corruption, absent versus unobserved touched facts, replay before changed Fresh query/policy, known abort/no mutation, Uncertain fencing and actual fault/kill/reconcile oracles. Existing source case/setup/both-host duties remain; a mathematically equivalent scoped leaf does not claim the complete original parent/runtime case.

Separate decoder/policy-projection/touched-reduction time from end-to-end same-writer disk read plus Immediate commit. Keep fixture creation, source hashing, ordinary open/recovery and oracle serialization outside the hot interval unless they are the explicitly named startup benchmark. Record whether close/Drop is inside: engine cleanup can allocate or perform I/O even when a first-party preflight refuses, as the actual Stage calibration already demonstrated. Never attribute an fsync-dominated improvement to allocation theory. Use valid supported profiles, including substantial valid policy and short/large valid composed scopes,0/1MiB payloads, small/large request limits and exact/tight R/S/C/W. Report semantic counts separately from physical visited rows/bytes, seeks/probes, schema work and returned/mutated rows. A future new counter/backend/profiler hook needs its own concrete approval; source inspection counts are not native measured events.

For every baseline/candidate, record exact commit/toolchain/build flags, allocator, engine/cache configuration, filesystem, OS/kernel, CPU/ISA, storage, concurrency, thermal/load state, dataset and distributions. Use the same complete correctness/workspace oracles and paired repeated A/B runs with order varied; report sample counts, median/p95/p99 latency, throughput and dispersion rather than one best result. Distinguish engine-cache warm, engine-cache disabled/cold, reopen and OS page-cache state. Reopening or cache0 alone does not establish an OS-cold run. Dataset/cache pressure may be measured and labeled without claiming controlled cold-cache equivalence. Profile allocations/peak live first-party ownership separately from engine pages, file mappings, allocator retention, RSS and on-disk growth/reclamation. Sparse relevant results and large unrelated prefixes/lane depth are independent axes, not one favorable dense workload.

Run the same recipe independently on real macOS and Linux, with each host's own correctness/cold/crash verification. The primary [Linux perf tutorial](https://perfwiki.github.io/main/tutorial/) supports counting and sampled profiling; document available events, user/kernel mode and enabled/running time when multiplexed. CPU-specific cycles/events are not directly comparable across different ISAs. On macOS use the official [performance and metrics guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/performance-and-metrics) and [performance investigation guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/improving-your-app-s-performance) for Time Profiler, Allocations and File Activity. Apple's current pages were available through official search text but their direct page bodies were JavaScript-only in this environment; I do not claim a complete current manual fetch or an Instruments run. Sampling CPU, allocation instrumentation and I/O tracing can perturb each other, so keep plain latency runs separate from explanatory profiles. For a future pure microbenchmark, [std::hint::black_box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/hint/fn.black_box.html) is only a best-effort optimization barrier, not correctness or a constant-time guarantee. Linux results cannot be inferred from the actual Darwin native acceptance, and logical admitted bytes cannot establish a speed/RSS gain on either host.

Claim preserves attempts and uses checked version/fence increments, so a healthy predecessor atMAX-1 can produceMAX. The source-derived token must represent that complete fence. No existing restoration rule requires created_at<=updated_at; independently valid restored DATA must not be refused by inventing that relationship. The FWCR original_time argument is actual retained metadata, not a current state clock or neighboring-row substitute. Shared type/worker/deadline and every row.updated_at==original_time remain explicit frozen obligations.

Typed partition and record IDs are nonempty binary<=65535, independently of the inline-value profile. workflow/admission::record_bytes includes ID length in its aggregate but applies check_value only to type/state/run_state/worker/token/optionals; PartitionId is independently typed. Actual Claim guard_due/guard_lane likewise treats ID/partition as typed. Explicit query filter components narrow to min(65535,inline), but Any can reach an actual longer partition without such a filter. A narrower operational profile must not become Corrupt, nor may impossible hard grammar be converted to a healthy profile refusal. Root independently selected the same distinction.

Allocation-free canonical token equality can reuse the actual source_token algorithm without constructing a LeaseToken or formatting String. Validate supplied field lengths first; remove exactly the already-known worker prefix from token, require one colon, compare canonical decimal original_time generated in one fixed20-byte stack array, require the next colon, compare full-u64 fence digits generated in the same reusable array, and require EOF. Decimal zero is exactly0; no plus sign, leading zero, extra delimiter or trailing byte is accepted. Worker itself may contain colon, NUL or invalidUTF8, so delimiter splitting/text parsing is incorrect. Direct equality against canonical generated digits also avoids a second integer parser and its overflow/normalization decisions. The current source-token implementation already uses modulo/division and stack20; no dependency or new scratch-owner model is needed.
